subject: Request: Transition carveout + staged ramp/smoothing proposal

Subject: Request for limited unwind carveout and ramp smoothing

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the fast responses last week. We ran this internally and have two asks before Procurement can sign: a short early-termination carveout tied to an acquisition contingency (12 months max), and a staged ramp-down schedule so we don’t face a hard billing cliff if usage drops post-PoC.

Specifically: can Redwood include language that allows a 6–12 month phased ramp in the event of a strategic divestiture, with proportional credits rather than an immediate full early-termination charge? We’re fine with a modest transactional fee but need predictable stages and a defined notice window.

I attached the draft we circulated (see attached redline). Can you route this to your deal desk/finance/legal and let us know what approvals you’d need?

Tom Alvarez

Ask: what’s the legal-safe carveout wording we can offer that keeps exposure capped and avoids setting a precedent for unlimited opt-outs? Finance, can you model an example credit schedule (3-step: 100% -> 60% -> 30% over 6 months) and show P&L impact on DG-4821? I’ve attached their redline.

Markus — reviewed NexGen’s redline. My quick read: we can agree to a limited ‘staggered unwind’ clause with the following guardrails:

- Trigger is a defined corporate event (change of control or divestiture of >50% of business line) with supporting evidence and a 30-day notice period.
- Maximum duration: 12 months.
- Credits are tied to committed MRR/ARR and amortized over the ramp window; we will require a slim termination fee (one-time administrative fee equal to 5% of the remaining committed value) and a proportional credit schedule.
- No access to cached customer data in the free-credit period; standard data export/retention terms apply.

I’m attaching a redline with alternative phrasing that keeps indemnity language intact and preserves our right to suspend service for non-payment. I also flagged language that would create an open-ended opt-out (we should not accept ‘at customer discretion’ wording).

Attachment: NexGen-Terms-Redline-v3.pdf

Marissa Cole
Head, Legal — Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference

Attached is a sample staged-ramp schedule and the headline impact for DG-4821 if we accept the 6/12 month taper with a 5% admin fee:

- If we run a 6-month staged ramp (100% month 0, 70% month 1-2, 40% month 3-4, 10% month 5-6), expected recognized ARR loss vs. committed = ~11%.
- If 12-month taper, recognized ARR loss = ~16% but cash burn smoothing improves by ~22% in the first 3 months.
- Credit uplift: propose limiting total concession to 18% of committed contract value without exec waiver. Any concession > 18% requires Laura’s sign-off.

I’ll attach the spreadsheet models. We should give NexGen a single ‘option election’ at signature (they choose 6- or 12-month ramp) and include a hard cap. Also recommend requiring a 30-day formal notice and verification materials.

Subject: Re: Request for limited unwind carveout and ramp smoothing — Executive approval to proceed

Tom / NexGen team — thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the redline. We have reviewed internally. Redwood can offer a controlled ‘staggered unwind’ carveout with the following final terms (executive-approved):

1) Election at signature: customer may elect either a 6-month or 12-month staged ramp schedule.
2) 30-day formal notice required, with supporting evidence of the triggering corporate event.
3) Administration fee: one-time 5% of remaining committed value charged at notice.
4) Credit schedule (examples; final values to be applied to the contract at signature):
   - 6-month option: billing taper: 100% (month 0) -> 70% (month 1–2) -> 40% (month 3–4) -> 10% (month 5–6)
   - 12-month option: more gradual taper; maximum concession capped at 18% of committed contract value without further waiver.
5) Data & access: standard export window; no free access to cached model outputs beyond retention policy.
6) Precedence: clause includes a one-time carveout limit per customer and is narrowly scoped to divestiture/change-of-control events only.

Markus — please send NexGen the attached staged-ramp spreadsheet and the redlined terms. Offer the 6- or 12-month election at signature and include the DocuSign link for the amendment. Laura has approved any concession up to 18% per the finance analysis; anything beyond requires further executive review.

Tom — attaching the redline and the ramp schedule. If that looks acceptable, we’ll generate an amendment + DocuSign (link below).
